# Run Driver (`tkt run`)

`core/run.py` executes the SDLC pipeline headlessly: **one phase per harness
invocation**, looping until a gate, a STOP signal, or a cap. It is the only part of
`tkt` that invokes an agent. It performs no VCS operations and bypasses no adapter
verb — it orchestrates invocations and ticket state, nothing else.

Entry points: `tkt run [KEY]`, `tkt run KEY --status`, `tkt run KEY --stop`, plus
`--max-iterations N` and `--dry-run`.

## Phases

Twelve, advanced in order:

```
P0   select-ticket      P4   self-review        P8   deploy-preview
P1   triage             P5   open-pr            P9   qa_ready   ← always a gate
P1.5 type-route         P6   ci-fix             P10  deploy-ready ← gated by config
P2   plan               P7   respond-to-review
P3   implement/test
```

A run started without a KEY begins at P0 and expects the harness to return a
`ticket_key`; with a KEY it begins at P1. If P0 advances without a `ticket_key` the
driver halts rather than guessing.

## The harness contract

[`build_phase_prompt()`](mex://function:22f0bcd3a241576f6745a79fa5b240e9) constructs
the prompt: it names the ticket, the phase, the attempt number, and instructs the agent
to execute **exactly one phase** per `skills/automated-sdlc/SKILL.md`, write
`result.json` into the state dir, and exit.

```json
{"phase":"P3","outcome":"advance|retry|blocked|gate","next":"P4","reason":"..."}
```

- `advance` — write a marker, move to `next`, reset attempt to 1
- `retry` — write a marker, re-run the same phase, attempt += 1
- `blocked` — transition the ticket to `blocked` and exit 1
- `gate` — write a marker and exit 0

A **missing or invalid `result.json` counts as a `retry`**, not a crash. This is
deliberate: a harness that dies mid-phase burns an attempt rather than the run.

`[run].harness_cmd` is a shell template containing `{prompt}`; the driver
single-quote-escapes the prompt and substitutes it. `harness_cmd` is **required** —
[`RunConfig`](mex://class:f506988f472b5d267840a7e0381ef825) raises a `ConfigError`
with an example if it is unset. The other `[run]` keys default to
`max_iterations = 30`, `max_phase_attempts = 3`, `invocation_timeout = 3600`.

## Gates — checked before invocation, not after

[`_loop()`](mex://method:78cd1c8af0c22f9f572d8a63a11c51f2) runs every stop condition
*before* spending an invocation. In order: STOP file, iteration cap, per-phase attempt
cap, then the three gates.

- **P9 is unconditional.** `is_gate_phase()` returns true for P9 and nothing else;
  human QA always stops the run.
- **P10 is opt-in.** [`is_production_phase()`](mex://function:7cb6f3e392bf881b6e220bc6b9339040)
  blocks P10 unless `[board.ownership]` sets `"deploy_ready->done" = "agent"`. The
  default when the key is absent is `human`, so production deploys never happen by
  omission.
- **Any human-owned transition halts.** [`is_human_owned_transition()`](mex://function:106e5c26e68da81cfaeb8e20162237c7)
  looks up `"<from_role>-><to_role>"` in `[board.ownership]`; a value of `human` stops
  the run before the phase executes.

Exceeding `max_phase_attempts` transitions the ticket to `blocked` and exits 1.
Exceeding `max_iterations` exits 1 without transitioning. A STOP file exits 0.

## State and resume

State lives at `.sdlc/state/run/<KEY>/`, resolved by
[`_state_dir()`](mex://function:b501118586fa02e1b3267a0a572d8d9d) relative to the
project root (the parent of the `.sdlc/` holding the config). It contains
`result.json` (the per-invocation handoff, deleted once read), `marker.json` (the
local resume mirror), `run.log` (appended per iteration), and `STOP` when halted.

Each phase also appends a comment to the ticket carrying a human line plus a
machine-readable `<!-- tkt-run: {...} -->` marker. The comment is authoritative —
it survives a lost worktree and is readable from another machine.

The catch, and the reason
[`read_ticket_marker()`](mex://function:5a5b4f21946edff1749db8729890cdb0) looks the way
it does: **the verb contract has no "list comments" verb**, and only the markdown
adapter exposes raw comment bodies (`_read_raw`). So the reader tries the adapter
first and falls back to `marker.json`. Remove that fallback and a resume on
Jira/GitHub/Linear silently restarts at P1 and redoes work. Conversely, a failed
mirror write is swallowed on purpose — the comment already landed, and losing resume
fidelity on one machine must not abort a run.

[`_resume_from_marker()`](mex://method:709e3d223e13067258000c76cb17c399) turns the last
marker back into position: `advance` → the recorded `next` with attempt 1; `retry` →
the same phase with attempt + 1; `blocked`/`gate`/unknown → resume exactly where it
stopped. No marker at all means a fresh run.

## Working on this subsystem

This is the one part of the codebase with real unit tests — `tests/test_run.py`
(34 tests) drives the whole state machine offline using the markdown adapter against
temp dirs and a stub harness script that writes scripted `result.json` sequences.
No model turns, no network. Any change here should be provable there first:

```sh
python3 -m unittest tests.test_run
```

`--dry-run` prints the command that would be executed and returns without invoking
anything, which is the safe way to check prompt construction and `harness_cmd`
substitution against a real config.
